posts.name: Vijay Anand
posts.cooked:
I have noticed that most of the assignments in BPT2 are around text processing. Isnt it is a bit more easier to use python to do such things, rather than depending on bash? How does one decide where to use bash, and where to use other languages like python?

I just couldnt stop thinking that the solution could have been more elegant / easier writing in python than bash.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Hello Phaedrus,

Yes, most real world scenarios have multiple possible solutions to a problem, some better/elegant than others. Many text processing tasks can be done using multiple tools like python, perl, awk, etc. In fact, for most text processing perl is way more powerful than python. However, the goal of this course is to equip you with yet another set of tools, bash, grep, sed, awk, and other GNU coreutils, so you can have option and expertise to use those whereever applicable. Further bash has the advantage of scriptability on all Unix based Operating Systems, whether python is installed there or not (you wont have super-user access on all servers to install whatever you want). Further if you are comfortable with bash or zsh, you can combine any and all tools like awk, perl, python, sed, etc into each other to solve the issue.

The goal of this course is to teach you the unix way of problem solving, using pipes and the “do one thing and do it well” philosophy.

posts.name: Vijay Anand
posts.cooked: That is a very valid perspective. Thank you for sharing @sayan ji
